films.title: Antigone
films.description: Javellas' Creon is the law that will not bend — the uncle-king who walls Antigone alive and learns too late what the gods require.

films.title: Oedipus the King
films.description: Saville keeps Creon as the brother-in-law under suspicion — the future king already waiting in Sophocles' first Theban play.

music.title: Oedipus Rex
music.description: Stravinsky's Creon brings the Delphic word and the political edge — the brother of Jocasta as the state answering the plague.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger's Creon is the decree itself set to music — the king who forbids the burial and pays with his house.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' Creon forbids the burial and walls Antigone alive — the uncle-king whose decree becomes Western drama's type of rigid state law.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Jean Anouilh
popCulture.description: Anouilh's Creon argues like a collaborator-administrator — reasonable, exhausted, and still the man who will kill the girl for order.
